Based on the search results, here's what you need to know about registering a phone number with WhatsApp Cloud API when it's already in use with a personal WhatsApp app:

## Key Issue

When you try to register a phone number for WhatsApp Cloud API that's already connected to an existing WhatsApp account, you'll get an error because a phone number can only be linked to one WhatsApp account at a time, and it cannot be used again for onboarding until it is disconnected from the current account.

## What Happens to Your Personal App

Once a phone number is registered on the WhatsApp Business API, it can't be used for WhatsApp Business or the WhatsApp consumer app. Registered numbers can still be used for everyday purposes, such as calling and text messages, but cannot be used with WhatsApp Messenger.

## How to Migrate Your Number

If the phone number you want to use for the WhatsApp Business API is already registered on WhatsApp (consumer or Business app), you must delete the existing account to free up the number for API registration.

To migrate a number, you must first delete the WhatsApp Messenger or WhatsApp Business App account. If you delete your WhatsApp Business app phone number and then register it for use with Cloud API, your existing messaging history will be lost, and you will be unable to use that number with the WhatsApp Business app again, unless you deregister the number from Cloud API.

## Alternative Option

You can create a WABA with a phone number that is already registered in the WhatsApp Business App without deleting the existing account through certain partners that support business app number onboarding, and you can send messages at scale using the WhatsApp Business API while maintaining one-on-one messaging in the WhatsApp Business App.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about WhatsApp Cloud API messaging tiers and rate limits:

## Messaging Tiers

New unverified accounts start at 250 unique contacts per day. After completing Business Verification, accounts can reach 1,000, then progress to 10,000, 100,000, and ultimately unlimited, all based on maintaining a high quality rating and consistent sending volume.

## What Counts as a Messaging Limit

A WhatsApp messaging limit is not the number of messages you can send; it is the number of unique customers you can start a new conversation with in a rolling 24-hour window. User-initiated conversations — where the customer messages you first — are effectively unlimited regardless of tier, because you are responding to demand, not pushing outreach.

## Tier Upgrades

To move from Tier 1 (1,000 limit) to Tier 2 (10,000 limit), your business must message at least 500 unique users within seven days. Meta evaluates your account every 6 hours to determine whether you qualify for the next messaging tier.

## Throughput (Speed Limits)

By default, the Cloud API handles 80 messages per second (mps). You can get an automatic throughput upgrade to 1,000 mps. To do this, you need an unlimited messaging tier. You must also send 100k messages in 24 hours.

## Embedded Signup Overview
WhatsApp Embedded Signup enables users to connect their WhatsApp Business accounts through Meta's streamlined OAuth flow without manual webhook configuration, significantly improving the user experience by automating the entire setup process.

The implementation involves six phases: Meta Account Setup (Create Developer Account + Business Manager), App Configuration (Create Business App, Add WhatsApp + Facebook Login, Record credentials), Embedded Signup (Configure OAuth, Add permissions, Integrate JS SDK, Exchange authorization code), Webhooks (Deploy HTTPS endpoint, Implement GET verification, Implement POST handler, Subscribe to required fields), Testing, and Production Activation.

The process includes registering the customer's business phone number for Cloud API use and subscribing your app to webhooks on the customer's WABA.

## Developer App Configuration
Administrators must configure environment variables for WHATSAPP_APP_ID (Facebook App ID), WHATSAPP_CONFIGURATION_ID (Configuration ID for Embedded Signup flow from Meta Developer Portal), and WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET (App Secret for token exchange).

## Webhook Setup Requirements
Before overriding the callback URI, your app must be subscribed to receive messages for the WhatsApp Business Account, which prevents error (#100) during webhook configuration, and the messages webhook field must be subscribed in your app's webhook settings.

# WhatsApp Cloud API Phone Number Registration

## Requirements & Steps

To register a business phone number for Cloud API, you must:

1. **Add** the number to your WhatsApp Business account via WhatsApp Manager

## 24-Hour Customer Service Window

When a customer messages your business first, a 24-hour customer service window opens, during which your team can reply with free-form messages at no additional Meta messaging cost. Each time the customer sends you a message, the 24-hour customer care window will restart.

## Free Service Conversations

Service messages are free-form replies sent inside the 24-hour customer service window after the customer initiates contact, and these messages are free under the current per-message model.

## Utility Templates

Utility templates sent in response to a customer inside the active 24-hour window are generally free, and these can include order updates, payment reminders, delivery alerts, or account notifications.

## Pricing Changes in July 2025

Effective July 1, 2025, Meta replaced conversation-based pricing with per-message pricing. Previously, one fee covered unlimited template messages sent within a 24-hour conversation window, but under the current model, each delivered template message is billed individually at a rate based on message category and recipient country. However, service messages and utility templates within open service windows remain free.

"Conversation pricing ended July 1, 2025" with per-message billing taking effect that same day.

**Yes, group messaging is supported.** The Groups API enables programmatic group creation and messaging through the WhatsApp Cloud API.

- **Required:** Businesses must have an "Official Business Account (OBA)"
- **Excluded:** "Groups are **not available** for WhatsApp Business app phone numbers and phone numbers onboarded to Multi-solution Conversations"
- **Capacity:** Maximum 8 participants per group, with a limit of 10,000 groups per business number

**Historical Support:** The provided documentation doesn't address whether groups were previously unavailable or when the feature initially launched.

**Message Type Limitations:** Supported types include text and media, but calling, disappearing messages, and interactive messages are excluded.

# WhatsApp Cloud API Setup Flow Summary

## Initial Setup
Begin by registering as a developer and creating a Meta app. The documentation states: "Click **Create App**" and "Select the **Connect with customers through WhatsApp** use case."

## Account Connection
Connect your Meta app to a WhatsApp Business account through the API Setup panel. You'll receive your WhatsApp Business account ID for subsequent API operations.

## Testing Phase
Generate a temporary access token to send test messages using a "From" phone number and recipient "To" number. After receiving a reply, you activate the customer service window—a 24-hour period permitting non-template messaging.

## Webhook Configuration
Set up a test webhook endpoint to receive message status notifications. The guide references: "You will need to set up a webhook endpoint in order to receive notifications about message statuses."

## Production Credentials
Navigate to Business Settings to create a system user and generate a permanent access token with specific permissions: `business_management`, `whatsapp_business_messaging`, and `whatsapp_business_management`.

## Message Sending
Use the Graph API endpoint with your permanent token to send non-template messages during active customer service windows, inserting your phone number ID and recipient details into the provided cURL command.

# WhatsApp Business Cloud API — Research Findings (as of July 2026)

## Setup Flow
- Setup requires a Meta developer account + a Meta app, created via "Create App" → select the "Connect with customers through WhatsApp" use case, then connect the app to a WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) in the API Setup panel, which yields the WABA ID. https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/get-started
- Testing uses a Meta-provided temporary test number + temporary access token; production requires creating a system user in Business Settings and generating a permanent token with scopes `business_management`, `whatsapp_business_messaging`, `whatsapp_business_management`. https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/get-started
- Embedded Signup is Meta's OAuth-based onboarding flow (JS SDK) that lets a business connect its WABA, register its business phone number for Cloud API, and auto-subscribe the app to webhooks without manual webhook config — recommended especially for solution/tech providers onboarding many businesses. https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/embedded-signup/overview
- Phone-number registration steps: add the number in WhatsApp Manager → verify ownership → call the registration endpoint with `"messaging_product":"whatsapp"` and a 6-digit `pin` (two-step verification PIN). Registration is limited to 10 requests per number in a 72-hour moving window (exceeding → error 133016, blocked 72h). https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-phone-numbers/registration

## Webhook Model
- Inbound messages arrive as HTTPS POST callbacks to a public endpoint you host. Setup requires a GET verification handshake (Meta sends `hub.challenge` + your configured verify token, which you echo back) plus a POST handler for message + status payloads; you must subscribe to the `messages` webhook field. https://developers.chatwoot.com/self-hosted/configuration/features/integrations/whatsapp-embedded-signup
- The app must be subscribed to receive messages for the WABA before overriding the callback URI (prevents error #100). https://developers.chatwoot.com/self-hosted/configuration/features/integrations/whatsapp-embedded-signup
- Outbound messages are sent via a Graph API POST to the phone-number-ID messages endpoint using the access token. https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/get-started

## Phone-Number Requirements (personal/normal WhatsApp app)
- A phone number can only be linked to one WhatsApp account at a time. To register a number already on the consumer WhatsApp or WhatsApp Business app for Cloud API, you must first delete that existing account to free the number. https://docs.rapidbott.com/help-center/platform/whatsapp-channel/connect-with-whatsapp-cloud-api/using-a-phone-number-already-in-use-with-whatsapp-app
- CONFIRMED: once registered to the Business/Cloud API, the number can no longer be used in the normal consumer WhatsApp app or the WhatsApp Business app. It still works for regular calls/SMS, but not WhatsApp Messenger. https://bitbybit.tawk.help/article/registering-a-new-phone-number-to-whatsapp-cloud-api
- Deleting the app account to migrate wipes that number's WhatsApp message history, and you cannot use it in the WhatsApp app again unless you deregister it from Cloud API. https://support.wati.io/en/articles/11463152-using-a-phone-number-in-wati-that-was-previously-registered-on-whatsapp
- Nuance: some BSP/partner flows ("Multi-solution Conversations" / business-app coexistence) let a number run on the API while keeping 1:1 chats in the WhatsApp Business app — but that is a special coexistence mode, not standard Cloud API registration. https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/solution-providers/migrate-existing-whatsapp-number-to-a-business-account/

## 24-Hour Customer-Service Window
- When a customer messages the business first, a 24-hour customer-service window opens during which the business can send free-form (non-template) replies. Every new inbound message from the customer resets the 24-hour clock. https://www.saysimple.com/blog/whatsapp-business-api-what-is-a-customer-care-window
- Free-form service replies inside the window are free under the current per-message model. Outside the window, you must use a pre-approved template to re-initiate. https://blueticks.co/blog/whatsapp-business-pricing-change-2026-per-message
- Entry-point windows: Click-to-WhatsApp ads / Facebook Page CTA taps open a 72-hour free messaging window. https://blueticks.co/blog/whatsapp-business-pricing-change-2026-per-message

## Template Messages & Pre-Approval
- Any business-initiated message sent outside an open service window must use a message template, which must be pre-approved by Meta and is categorized as Marketing, Utility, or Authentication. https://blueticks.co/blog/whatsapp-business-pricing-change-2026-per-message
- Under per-message pricing each delivered template is billed by its category and the recipient's country. https://blueticks.co/blog/whatsapp-business-pricing-change-2026-per-message

## 2026 Pricing — the per-conversation → per-MESSAGE shift
- Per-message pricing took effect July 1, 2025, replacing the old conversation-based model. Conversation-based pricing is now deprecated by Meta. https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/pricing/conversation-based-pricing
- Old model: one fee per 24-hour conversation covered unlimited templates in that window. New model: every delivered template is billed individually by category + recipient country. https://blueticks.co/blog/whatsapp-business-pricing-change-2026-per-message
- Current representative rates (US/default region, 2026):
  - Marketing ≈ $0.025/msg; Utility ≈ $0.004/msg; Authentication ≈ $0.004/msg; Service (free-form in-window replies) = free. https://blueticks.co/blog/whatsapp-business-pricing-change-2026-per-message
  - Utility templates delivered inside an open 24-hour service window are free; Authentication gets no free-window relief. https://blueticks.co/blog/whatsapp-business-pricing-change-2026-per-message
- Rates vary sharply by recipient country (follows the recipient's country code, not sender). Marketing examples: India ≈ $0.0094, Brazil ≈ $0.0625, US ≈ $0.025, UK ≈ $0.048, UAE ≈ $0.0499, Mexico ≈ $0.0305, Germany > $0.124. https://blueticks.co/blog/whatsapp-business-api-pricing-2026
- Free-tier change: the old "1,000 free service conversations/month" allowance was removed under per-message pricing; instead all service (free-form in-window) messages are free, with no monthly cap. https://www.ycloud.com/blog/whatsapp-api-pricing-update

## Group Messaging — UPDATED for 2026 (correction to the old assumption)
- The premise "Cloud API does NOT support groups" is now OUTDATED. Meta shipped a Groups API, now open to all businesses with an Official Business Account (OBA) — it supports programmatic group creation and sending text/media to groups. https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/groups
- Restrictions: max 8 participants per group, up to 10,000 groups per business number; not available for WhatsApp Business app numbers or numbers on Multi-solution Conversations; no calling, disappearing, or interactive messages in groups. https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/groups
- Practical caveat: this is a distinct Groups API gated behind OBA status — standard/basic Cloud API messaging to arbitrary existing consumer groups is still not a thing; you send only to API-managed groups. https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/groups/groups-messaging/

## Rate Limits / Messaging Tiers
- Messaging limit = number of unique customers you can start a new conversation with in a rolling 24-hour window (not total messages). User-initiated conversations are effectively unlimited regardless of tier. https://wetarseel.ai/whatsapp-api-rate-limits-messaging-tiers/
- Tiers: new unverified accounts start at 250 unique contacts/day → after Business Verification progress through 1K → 10K → 100K → unlimited, based on quality rating + volume. https://wetarseel.ai/whatsapp-api-rate-limits-messaging-tiers/
- Upgrade mechanics: to move 1K → 10K you must message ≥500 unique users in 7 days; Meta re-evaluates every ~6 hours. https://wetarseel.ai/whatsapp-api-rate-limits-messaging-tiers/
- Throughput (separate from tiers): Cloud API defaults to 80 messages/sec, auto-upgradable to 1,000 mps once you reach unlimited tier and send 100k messages in 24h. https://www.wuseller.com/whatsapp-business-knowledge-hub/scale-whatsapp-cloud-api-master-throughput-limits-upgrades-2026/

---

## Sources

- [Meta – Register a business phone number](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/business-phone-numbers/registration)
- [Meta – Embedded Signup Overview](https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/business-messaging/whatsapp/embedded-signup/overview)

- [Wati – Using a number previously registered on WhatsApp](https://support.wati.io/en/articles/11463152-using-a-phone-number-in-wati-that-was-previously-registered-on-whatsapp)
- [Saysimple – What is a Customer Care Window](https://www.saysimple.com/blog/whatsapp-business-api-what-is-a-customer-care-window)
- [Blueticks – Per-message pricing change 2026](https://blueticks.co/blog/whatsapp-business-pricing-change-2026-per-message)
- [Blueticks – WhatsApp API pricing 2026 (rates by market)](https://blueticks.co/blog/whatsapp-business-api-pricing-2026)
- [YCloud – Pricing update effective July 1, 2025](https://www.ycloud.com/blog/whatsapp-api-pricing-update)
- [Wetarseel – Rate limits & messaging tiers](https://wetarseel.ai/whatsapp-api-rate-limits-messaging-tiers/)
- [Wuseller – Throughput limits & upgrades 2026](https://www.wuseller.com/whatsapp-business-knowledge-hub/scale-whatsapp-cloud-api-master-throughput-limits-upgrades-2026/)

---

### Two flags for you
1. **Group messaging assumption is now wrong.** As of 2026 Meta has a Groups API (OBA accounts only, max 8 participants/group, API-managed groups only). If your architecture depended on "Cloud API can't do groups," that premise needs revisiting — though it still can't message arbitrary existing consumer groups.
2. **The phone-number one-way door is confirmed** — registering a number to Cloud API removes it from the normal WhatsApp/Business app (history lost, reversible only by deregistering). Relevant to any pilot that reuses a personal number. A BSP coexistence mode is the only exception.

Meta's own docs are terse on the "removed from normal app" point (third-party BSP docs state it most explicitly); everything else is anchored to primary Meta documentation.
